title: Your first Node script
idea: A Node script is a JavaScript file you run from the terminal with the `node` command, no browser or web page needed.
points: Node reads the file and runs it from the first line to the last.
`console.log` writes a line to standard output, which your terminal shows.
Node exits after the last line, unless work is still pending, like a timer.
`console.error` writes to standard error, a separate stream for errors.

parts.label: Program
parts.note: Starts the Node.js runtime, which then loads your file.

parts.label: File name
parts.note: Any name you choose. Node looks for it in the folder where you typed the command.

parts.label: Extension
parts.note: Marks an ES module, so `import` works. This book uses `.mjs`; the modules page explains it.

parts.label: Argument
parts.note: Extra words after the file name. Your script reads them from `process.argv`, starting at index 2.

code.title: Hello, world
code.caption: Run it here, then change the greeting. In a terminal, add a name after the file name to greet someone else.

code.title: When it exits
code.caption: The last line runs, yet the timer still fires: Node waits for pending work before it exits.

pitfalls: Run `node` in the file's folder, or pass its path; else you get `Cannot find module`.
Write the whole file name: `node hello` does not find `hello.mjs`.
Add the file name: `node` alone opens an interactive prompt; type `.exit` to leave it.

quiz.q: What does `node greet.mjs Ada Lovelace` print?
quiz.why: `process.argv[0]` is the path to `node`, `[1]` is the script's path, and the first argument sits at index 2.

takeaway: Node runs the file you name, then waits only for pending work.
